title: The verse passed on
hook: Upatissa hears Assaji's verse, understands, and runs to tell Kolita (Vinaya, Mahavagga 1)

segments.voice: Yesterday, a pact, and your line: whoever finds it first. Did you make one promise to a friend, and mean it? Today, one of the two friends finds it. Day seven hundred twenty-seven.

Kolita sees his friend coming from a distance, and something has already changed. Not a word has been said yet. It's in Upatissa's face. The Vinaya, the monks' book of discipline, tells the scene simply: Kolita notices that his friend looks calm and clear, and asks him straight out whether he has found the deathless, the thing they both left home to look for. And Upatissa says yes. Earlier on this path we followed Upatissa through the streets of Rajagaha behind a quiet monk named Assaji and heard the short verse Assaji gave him. Today is the other half of that morning: what Upatissa did with it.
screen: `A CHANGED FACE.` → `HAVE YOU FOUND IT?` → `YES, FRIEND.`

segments.voice: Start with where he went. Upatissa had just understood the thing he had left home to look for. He could have stayed to question Assaji. He could have gone straight to find the Buddha. Instead he went to Kolita, because that was the pact. The verse was small enough to carry at a run. In paraphrase: of things that arise from a cause, the Buddha has told the cause, and also how they cease. Next, notice what he passed on. Not his own summary. Not a better version. He gave Kolita the same lines he'd heard, and the text says that on hearing them, Kolita understood too. Same words, second friend. Then they thought of someone else. Their old teacher, Sanjaya, still led a crowd of students. So the two friends went back and invited him to come with them. He refused, and offered instead to share the leadership of his group with them. They said no to that, and left, and the Vinaya says many of his students went with them. What they had found was offered even to the teacher who had stopped being enough for them. Last, the arrival. The text says the Buddha saw the two friends coming from far off and told the monks, in paraphrase: these two will be my chief pair of disciples. Upatissa would be called Sariputta, and Kolita, Moggallana. Here's what the story keeps doing. Every person in it who finds something good turns around and hands it on. Assaji to Upatissa. Upatissa to Kolita. Both of them to their old teacher. The verse travels because nobody sits on it.
screen: `HE WENT TO KOLITA FIRST.` · `THE SAME VERSE, UNCHANGED.` · `BACK TO THE OLD TEACHER.` · `THE CHIEF PAIR ARRIVES.` · then, large: `HE RAN TO TELL HIM.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pass on something good. Settle, and let the breath slow down. Go back over the last week and find one thing that helped you. A sentence someone said. A song. A recipe that worked. A way to fix a sticky door. Just one. Now find the person who would want it. Bring their face to mind, the way Kolita saw his friend's face before a word was said. Don't polish the thing or add to it. Decide only how it gets to them: a message, a call, a note on the counter. Then rest with the breath until the end. The bell holds the time.
Deathless. The thing Upatissa tells Kolita he has found, after hearing Assaji's short verse and understanding it. Today's word.
Your line: he ran to tell him. Today, when something good finds you, hand it to someone the same day, before it cools. Day seven hundred twenty-seven.

screen: `DAY 727 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE GENERAL OF THE DHAMMA.`

howItsDone: Assaji's verse is recited in Buddhist communities as a summary of the teaching, and the story of the two friends is told at temples and in Dhamma talks as the beginning of the Buddha's chief pair of disciples.

match.prompt: who passed what to whom: tap the pairs.

myth: Upatissa went straight to the Buddha after hearing the verse
he went first to Kolita, because of their pact.
Kolita needed the verse explained at length
he heard the same lines and understood too.

Sanjaya refused, but many of his students went along.

fork.setup: you're Upatissa and Kolita. you've found what you were looking for, and your old teacher Sanjaya still leads a crowd of students. what do you do?
options: slip away quietly and say nothing.
go back and invite him to come with you.
stay and win over his students yourselves.
fork.reveal: they go back and invite him. he refuses and offers them a share in leading his group instead. they leave, and many of his students go with them.

original.note: Pali: 'the things that arise from a cause', the opening words of Assaji's verse.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story about one famous verse.
what it means: the verse works twice. Upatissa hears it from Assaji, gives the same words to Kolita, and it works again.
what a scholar hears: in the Vinaya the story sits in the opening narrative of the Mahavagga, which tells how the order of monks first grew.

sources.ref: Vinaya Pitaka, Mahavagga 1.23–24 (Sariputta and Moggallana: the verse, the pact kept, Sanjaya, the arrival)

notes: All Vinaya material paraphrased. Confirm in Mahavagga 1.23–24 (Rhys Davids and Oldenberg, SBE 13): Moggallana notices Sariputta's serene face and asks whether he has reached the deathless; Sariputta repeats Assaji's verse and Moggallana understands; they invite Sanjaya, who refuses and offers to share leadership; Sanjaya's students go with them; the Buddha sees them from afar and names them his chief pair.
Script says 'many of his students' rather than the number the Vinaya gives (two hundred fifty), per the claims rule; the text's own number could be restored if wanted.
The Vinaya also says Sanjaya vomited hot blood when his students left; omitted as needlessly harsh for this angle.
Day 68 (year one) told the Assaji meeting itself and the verse's spread in inscriptions; this day deliberately takes the second half of the morning instead.
Original: confirm Devanagari and the transliteration 'ye dhamma hetuppabhava'; stress marking is approximate.
Editor: cut 'spent years chasing' (unsupported duration), replaced 'good news' with neutral wording, and fixed the garbled practice line about Kolita seeing his friend's face.
